decisions.quote: We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
decisions.reason: In the supplied abstract, the conservatism–life satisfaction association ('Why are conservatives happier than liberals?') is introduced as the baseline phenomenon ('this effect') to be explained, not as the specific claim attributed to Napier and Jost (2008). What the text attributes to Napier and Jost (2008) is the explanatory mediation claim: they 'argue that this is because conservative ideology has a palliative (system-justifying) function that protects conservatives’ (but not liberals’) happiness,' which the authors later explicitly refer to as 'Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.' Observing in the new sample (N = 816) that conservatives are more satisfied with life than liberals establishes the baseline direct relationship required to test competing mediation pathways (the authors' SES/group-membership pathway versus Napier and Jost's system-justifying ideology pathway), rather than constituting a separate replicated finding framed as partial agreement. Under the codebook, 'mixed' is used only when the authors themselves frame their evidence as partly supporting and partly not supporting the original, and the central-finding/preliminary-check rules specify coding the central finding the replication was designed to test (where a preliminary prerequisite that holds followed by a failed main test is still 'failed'). Because the only finding attributed to Napier and Jost and re-tested as the central replication target explicitly failed to replicate, the outcome is 'failed'.

scope_review.parent_objection: The first reply codes failed from explicit failure of system-justifying-ideology mediation. But abstract states original problem Why are conservatives happier than liberals? Napier/Jost argue this is because ideology protects happiness, and current study finds conservatives more satisfied while mediation fails. Is conservatism-life-satisfaction association itself a tested original finding satisfying implicit comparison criteria, giving mixed, or merely background/preliminary premise around the central original mediation claim, giving failed? Explicit failure of one mediation is not automatically overall verdict on all original findings under Rule1. Follow exact central-finding rule and tested-original-comparison rule without inventing additional original hypotheses. Explain empirical scope and original finding evidence; no third call.
